unit_description: This unit introduces multiplication through equal groups. Students count groups, connect repeated addition to multiplication, and identify factors and products in multiplication situations.
unit_goals: Write multiplication equations for equal groups.

weeks.weekly_focus: Students explore multiplication as equal groups, connect repeated addition, and learn the meanings of factor and product.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by counting by twos, threes, and fives.
lessons.concept: Multiplication begins with equal groups. If you have 4 groups of 3, you can count 3, 6, 9, 12 or multiply 4 times 3.
lessons.practice: Count the total number of items in equal groups using skip counting.
lessons.objective: Count equal groups and find totals using skip counting.

questions.prompt: How many wheels are on 3 cars?

learn.title: Count Equal Groups
teaching_points: A group has the same number of items.
Skip counting is faster than counting by ones.

example.prompt: How many apples are in 3 baskets of 5?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: There are 4 boxes with 4 crayons each. How many crayons total?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Count the total number of items in each set of equal groups.

bigIdea.title: Count Equal Groups
bigIdea.subtitle: Skip count to find the total
bigIdea.intro: Equal groups are the foundation of multiplication. Skip counting helps you find the total without counting one by one.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why is skip counting helpful for equal groups?

ruleCards.description: Every group must have the same number of items.
Count by the number in each group to find the total.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by writing repeated addition sentences for groups.
lessons.concept: Repeated addition is the same as multiplication. 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 4 × 3. The first factor tells how many groups, the second tells how many in each group.
lessons.practice: Write multiplication equations for repeated addition sentences and pictures.
lessons.objective: Connect repeated addition to multiplication equations.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by matching repeated addition to multiplication.

learn.title: Connect Repeated Addition to Multiplication
teaching_points: Repeated addition adds the same number again and again.
Multiplication is a shortcut for repeated addition.
The first factor is the number of groups; the second is the group size.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Change each repeated addition into a multiplication equation.

flashcards.title: Repeated Addition vs Multiplication
flashcards.instructions: Review how repeated addition and multiplication are related.

bigIdea.title: Connect Repeated Addition to Multiplication
bigIdea.subtitle: Multiplication is a faster way to add the same number
bigIdea.intro: Instead of writing 3 + 3 + 3 + 3, you can write 4 × 3. Both mean 4 groups of 3.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How is multiplication like repeated addition?

ruleCards.description: Multiplication is a shorter way to show repeated addition.
The first factor tells how many groups there are.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by naming the parts of multiplication equations.
lessons.concept: In a multiplication equation like 3 × 5 = 15, the numbers being multiplied are factors and the answer is the product.
lessons.practice: Label factors and products in multiplication equations and word problems.
lessons.objective: Identify factors and products in multiplication.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by identifying parts of multiplication.

questions.hint: The factors are the numbers being multiplied.

questions.prompt: Which is bigger: the product or the factors?
questions.hint: The product is the total of all groups.

learn.title: Identify Factors and Products
teaching_points: Factors are the numbers being multiplied.
The product is the total or answer.
Each factor tells something about the groups.

example.prompt: In 5 × 4 = 20, name the factors and product.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.hint: The numbers being multiplied are factors.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Identify the factors and product in each equation.

bigIdea.title: Identify Factors and Products
bigIdea.subtitle: Name the parts of a multiplication equation
bigIdea.intro: Every multiplication equation has two factors and one product. The factors tell us about the groups, and the product is the total.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What do the two factors in a multiplication equation tell you?

ruleCards.description: The factors tell how many groups and how many are in each group.
The product is the total amount after combining the groups.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by drawing quick groups for given multiplication equations.
lessons.concept: A multiplication story can be drawn as equal groups, an array, or a number line. Drawing helps you see the factors and product.
lessons.practice: Draw and describe multiplication situations from equations and word problems.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by describing a multiplication situation.

questions.hint: 3 is the number of groups, 4 is the group size.

questions.prompt: There are 5 vases with 2 flowers each. Write the multiplication equation.

learn.title: Draw and Describe Multiplication Situations
teaching_points: Use circles or boxes to show groups.
The first factor is the number of groups.
The second factor is the size of each group.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Draw 3 groups of 5 and write the multiplication equation.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Draw a picture and write an equation for each multiplication situation.

flashcards.title: Drawing Multiplication
flashcards.instructions: Review words for drawing multiplication situations.

bigIdea.title: Draw and Describe Multiplication Situations
bigIdea.subtitle: Pictures make multiplication visible
bigIdea.intro: When you draw multiplication, you turn numbers into a picture. Each group is the same size, and the total is the product.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How can drawing help you understand multiplication?

ruleCards.description: Draw one circle for each group and put the same number of dots in each.
Use words to tell the same story as the equation.

lessons.fact_drill: Rapid review of counting equal groups, repeated addition, factors and products, and drawing multiplication.
lessons.concept: Review the four big ideas from this unit: equal groups, repeated addition, factors and products, and describing multiplication situations.
lessons.practice: Complete a balanced evaluation covering the skills from this unit.
lessons.objective: Show what you know about equal groups.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Get ready to show what you know.

learn.title: Ready to Show What You Know
teaching_points: Use any strategy that helps you.

example.prompt: You have learned four big ideas this unit.
example.equation: equal groups + repeated addition + factors/products + drawing = equal groups

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.hint: First factor is 4, second factor is 9.

practice_block.title: Unit Evaluation
practice_block.instructions: Answer all questions carefully to show your understanding.

flashcards.title: Unit 9 Review
flashcards.instructions: Review key terms from Unit 9 before the evaluation.

bigIdea.title: Unit Evaluation: Equal Groups
bigIdea.subtitle: Show what you know
bigIdea.intro: This evaluation checks your understanding of the four big ideas from this unit: counting equal groups, repeated addition, factors and products, and drawing multiplication situations.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What do you know about equal groups?

ruleCards.description: Multiplication is a faster way to add equal groups.
The first factor is groups; the second is group size; the answer is the product.
